title: The Green Guest Book  (Le livre d'or vert)

segments.t: À la table ensoleillée du coin café, Mademoiselle Evelyn chausse ses lunettes de lecture à côté de Hannah et d'Arthur et ouvre le registre toilé vert au mois de mai, trente ans plus tôt. Tendez d'abord l'oreille.
Look how neat every page is: date, room number, guest name, and weather.
Turn to May tenth, Miss Evelyn, the Friday written on our postcard!
Here it is! 'Heavy rain all night; water dripped onto the sunroom piano.'
Read the next line: 'Moved the piano to the dry corner; middle key swollen shut.'
Oh! That rainy night broke the roof and jammed middle D at the same time!
Look at my aunt's note underneath: 'Locked Room Nine until the roof is dry.'
And she tucked her unfinished waltz inside the lid to wait for sunny weather!
Then summer guests filled the house, years passed, and the bookcase went up.
She never got to hear the second half of her Friday waltz.
Arthur, with your permission, may I write the missing sixteen bars for Wednesday?
You would finish my aunt's song for our reopening, Miss Evelyn?!
In the very same key, with her opening melody leading us home.
Déchiffrons ensemble chaque ligne de ce vieux registre.
Look how neat every page is: date, room number, guest name, and weather.
'Regardez comme chaque page est soignée: date, numéro de chambre, nom du client et météo.'
Turn to May tenth, Miss Evelyn, the Friday written on our postcard!
'Ouvrez au dix mai, Mademoiselle Evelyn, le vendredi inscrit sur notre carte postale!'
Here it is! 'Heavy rain all night; water dripped onto the sunroom piano.'
'Nous y voilà! "Forte pluie toute la nuit; de l'eau a goutté sur le piano de la véranda."'
Read the next line: 'Moved the piano to the dry corner; middle key swollen shut.'
'Lisez la ligne suivante: "Déplacé le piano vers le coin sec; touche centrale gonflée et bloquée."'
Oh! That rainy night broke the roof and jammed middle D at the same time!
'Oh! Cette nuit de pluie a endommagé le toit et coincé le ré central en même temps!'
Look at my aunt's note underneath: 'Locked Room Nine until the roof is dry.'
'Regardez l'annotation de ma tante juste en dessous: "Fermé la chambre neuf à clé jusqu'à ce que le toit soit sec."'
And she tucked her unfinished waltz inside the lid to wait for sunny weather!
'Et elle a glissé sa valse inachevée sous le couvercle en attendant le retour du soleil!'
Then summer guests filled the house, years passed, and the bookcase went up.
'Puis les clients d'été ont rempli la maison, les années ont filé et la bibliothèque a été montée.'
She never got to hear the second half of her Friday waltz.
'Elle n'a jamais eu l'occasion d'entendre la seconde moitié de sa valse du vendredi.'
Arthur, with your permission, may I write the missing sixteen bars for Wednesday?
'Arthur, avec votre permission, puis-je écrire les seize mesures manquantes pour mercredi?'
You would finish my aunt's song for our reopening, Miss Evelyn?!
'Vous achèveriez le morceau de ma tante pour notre réouverture, Mademoiselle Evelyn?!'
In the very same key, with her opening melody leading us home.
'Dans la tonalité exacte, avec sa mélodie d'ouverture pour nous ramener à bon port.'
Écoutons à nouveau cet échange émouvant d'un bout à l'autre.

Turn to May tenth, Miss Evelyn, the Friday written on our postcard!

Oh! That rainy night broke the roof and jammed middle D at the same time!
Look at my aunt's note underneath: 'Locked Room Nine until the roof is dry.'
And she tucked her unfinished waltz inside the lid to wait for sunny weather!
Then summer guests filled the house, years passed, and the bookcase went up.
She never got to hear the second half of her Friday waltz.
Arthur, with your permission, may I write the missing sixteen bars for Wednesday?
You would finish my aunt's song for our reopening, Miss Evelyn?!
In the very same key, with her opening melody leading us home.
Le mystère de la véranda condamnée et de la partition inachevée est éclairci, et Mademoiselle Evelyn propose d'écrire la fin de la valse pour mercredi. À très vite!
See you later!
